rites.name: Ilyamiel
rites.text: Ilyamiel is the concept of the first sounding of Shyuthora, the note that drew the roots of the world together in the Singing before any calendar existed. In the Age of the first sovereign it is remembered as the hum beneath growing groves and young kingdoms, a pattern that holds soil and sky in tune.

rites.name: Crarnen
rites.text: Crarnen is the concept of the Courts of Shyuthora, the councils where the first sovereign's trials were judged and the doors between worlds were argued into being. It is remembered as the pattern that shaped the groves and growing kingdoms of that era.

rites.name: Thone
rites.text: Thone is a concept in Shyuthora, a principle of measured obligation that governed the courts of divine trials during the reign of the first sovereign. It was understood as the bond that held councils to their word and kept the doors between worlds from failing.

rites.name: Drestock
rites.text: Drestock is a concept in Shyuthora, the principle that a word spoken before the Courts binds the speaker's own flame to the doors between worlds. During the Holy Age its name was taken up by temple orders who tested their oaths against the trials of the council.

rites.name: Vorum
rites.text: A tactic in which a wanderer chooses to hold one spot and avoid open clashes. Many who share the roads consider it a clumsy habit of novices.

rites.name: Ceostantia
rites.text: A devotion practiced by humbling oneself before ancient sacred machines, followed by many within a broad faith that venerates the ones who came before. Adherents embrace sacrifice and simplicity as a path of reverence.

rites.name: Ceoleranum
rites.text: A mournful chant that rises when a warrior discovers his spouse slain by a rival under a zealot's command. It accompanies the moment grief turns into resolve.

rites.name: Ciriarnanum
rites.text: A descending technique where a traveler glides down a sheer ledge or wall by hugging its corner, avoiding harm from the fall. It works only on steep faces meeting at sharp or nearly flat-edged angles.

rites.name: Neoria Valausia
rites.text: A reckless trick where a traveler leaps onto a charging beast as it readies its strike, letting the blow hurl them across the land to reach hidden places.

rites.name: Caulanum Lanirnus
rites.text: A discipline of structured combat methods devised for battle, personal protection, or contest. Those who train in it are called fighters of the discipline.

rites.name: Telenor Molauror
rites.text: A sacred set of twelve precepts that a devout people chant in silent rhythm while swaying. Its teachings call for the return of stolen rites and a restored store of ancient wisdom.

rites.name: Sonum
rites.text: A sacred chant or verse sung in devotion, which followers may also speak as a prayer. Adherents of an ancient faith recite its stanzas to voice their belief.

rites.name: Thasora
rites.text: Thasora is a dormant stellar concept of the Shyuthora universe, a crystalline engine-lattice that was grown rather than built and rests in the cores of old suns. Its makers measured civilizations by how deeply they could draw on stellar fire, and Thasora itself was designed to be drawn upon in turn. In its seventh age it still answers only to those who can sing its harmonics back to it.

rites.name: Thassith
rites.text: Thassith is a sealed relic-engine that hums inside a shell of coiled light, kept dormant for seven ages until its keepers wake it. Its cold lattice holds five sleeping wardens in suspended stasis, and any attempt to open the shell risks a shockwave that could scorch a sector of stars.

rites.name: Oseithora
rites.text: Oseithora is a sovereign bureau of the Concord of Thessarine, tasked with apportioning the sunken relics of the vanished Lumen-builders among the Concord's many peoples. Its keepers have long been accused of hoarding the most potent artifacts for their own ascendant faction. Its former chief now presides over a rival faith that teaches the relics were never meant to be shared.

rites.name: Halostedon
rites.text: Halostedon is a concept of Shyuthora's Seeding, the quiet season when the makers plant the Weave and the sleeping powers lie dormant beneath the groves. It names the hush that settles over the growing kingdoms of the first sovereign, when every spark is kept low and rooted.

rites.name: Renes
rites.text: A flaw in a sealed rite lets a companion who was turned against just before a farewell scene remain present afterward. The fault is named for the first companion it kept alive, and the greater tale is left unchanged.

rites.name: Melleontum
rites.text: A contest where a chosen figure grants every nearby companion swiftness, fierceness, toughness, and regenerating shields and concealment. Bands that keep close together gain the most, though gathering makes them easy prey for blasts that strike many at once.

rites.name: Serirus Masus
rites.text: A duelist's method of moving through a rigid, repeating pattern so the fighter can mentally record how a rival blocks feints and strikes. Practitioners learn it from a renowned teacher within a fortified stronghold.

rites.name: Amiastia Tolanum
rites.text: A martial discipline in which a warrior fights while wielding two blades of pure energy at once. Skill in this art brings great honor and a reputation among the warrior caste.

rites.name: Sasteizeth
rites.text: Sasteizeth is a stellar-realm concept in Shyuthora's Era 4, a two-year-old coordinating council that oversees the command of every star-faring fleet and garrison across its territories. Its authority is divided between a ground-directing lattice and a naval wing, with regional lodges holding authority over their own sectors of drifting space. Its central hall was moved to a fortified orbital vault after an earlier seat was lost, and its strategy has guided every campaign since its founding.

rites.name: Zephasis
rites.text: Zephasis is a drifting stellar concept in the Shyuthora omniverse, a lattice of brightly burning filaments that the ancient wardens of the outer dust used to hold dying suns in careful balance. Its name is spoken by those who keep the old ledgers, where it marks the seventh turning of the age of embers.

rites.name: Vesishora
rites.text: Vesishora is a dormant solar-harvesting lattice that drifts in the outer shell of Shyuthora's primary star, waiting for a signal from the ancient keepers who built it. When awakened, it can gather the star's flares into a single lance of plasma that can tear through orbital defenses. Its units are seldom seen, yet every appearance marks a turning point in the local wars.

rites.name: Xaasseth
rites.text: Xaasseth is a stellar-scale concept in the Shyuthora omniverse, born in the fourth era and aged four ages. It is remembered as a patient instrument that waits unseen in the dark between suns, then strikes when a coordinated deployment of its kind is ready to move.

rites.name: Valesarnor
rites.text: A passing flaw in the workings of the land where a swift traveler slips straight through a solid barrier. It turns up across many realms and is said to take its name from an old word for walking through walls.

rites.name: Corelles
rites.text: A technique in which a wanderer leaps while a blast of force they have set off beneath them hurls them upward. The lift carries them to ledges and heights that a plain jump could never reach.

rites.name: Vinanum
rites.text: A precise strike aimed at a foe's skull, which ends a bare-headed opponent at once. Its narrow mark makes it hard to land, so skilled users rely on sighted tools to achieve it.

rites.name: Valiaseonia
rites.text: A small band or machine takes a high vantage to scan the ground ahead while allies advance. It gives covering fire and warns of hidden foes lurking in likely positions.

rites.name: Viastiles
rites.text: A quirk in the mechanics of a bearer's craft that lets a weapon keep discharging while the world is held still. The effect persists until the pause is lifted.

rites.name: Serellanum
rites.text: A quirk of the mesh allows a wielder to strike a foe using a backup arm in place of the usual blade. Pressing two controls together triggers it, though some halls may refuse the trick.

rites.name: Raulleorus
rites.text: A ruinous tactic where many unguided munitions are dropped in a dense blanket over an entire region. It aims to wipe out soldiers and supplies or to break the will of those below.

rites.name: Neontum Liraunium
rites.text: A craft of spreading messages to sway a crowd toward a chosen aim. It bends truths, favors bold feeling over careful reasoning, and reduces hard questions to simple sigils and slogans.

rites.name: Relles
rites.text: A stealth technique where a fighter approaches an unaware foe from behind and triggers a dramatic, instantly lethal strike. It can be used in both solo ventures and contests between many combatants.

rites.name: Lestanum
rites.text: A proficiency mark earned by bringing down a winged flying craft mid-air using hurled explosives or a shoulder-fired launcher. Its emblem is a golden ring enclosing a violet winged vessel.

rites.name: Rialles
rites.text: A recognition given to a participant whenever they earn a retaliation medal during shared combat play. Each occurrence grants one point toward the tally.

rites.name: Mellintum
rites.text: A clever technique that lets a traveler bypass the main route through a fortified command chamber. It can be carried out on a specific stage of the campaign to skip ahead.

rites.name: Vauliarium
rites.text: A hidden flaw in one arena lets a flying craft hang motionless in the air. Only that particular battleground allows the trick to be performed.

rites.name: Coraures
rites.text: A shared rite where up to four companions join together through a summoning circle. They fight as one band against the same foes.

rites.name: Serianus
rites.text: A timing trick lets a wielder make a thrown bomb vanish mid-flight without ever going off. Anyone who learns the exact moment to act can cancel the blast entirely.

rites.name: Oreosiania
rites.text: A practiced handling trick where a warrior presses two keys in quick succession to delay a weapon's refill. Skilled users chain several shots before the automatic reload begins.

rites.name: Amiarnontes
rites.text: A skilled user pushes a projectile or explosive off its path by setting off a blast nearby. The trick gains extra distance or hides a shot around a corner, leaving opponents bewildered.

rites.name: Lintor
rites.text: A reward earned by crushing twenty foes beneath a heavy armored machine's stomping strike. It marks a warrior who has mastered the crushing blow.

rites.name: Liastasium
rites.text: A tally earned each time a fighter downs a foe using a precise long-range arm during contests. It is shown as a plain blue emblem marked with a crosshair.

rites.name: Launia
rites.text: A traveler folds their legs tight while leaping, shrinking their outline so they can clear higher ledges and slip through narrow openings. In some tales it also softens the shock of a hard landing.

rites.name: Meleonanum
rites.text: A flaw in a projection craft makes a phantom figure appear without a body to imitate. The phantom may wear plain or random gear, and each observer sees different garments.

rites.name: Maurnoria
rites.text: A chained sequence of inputs that, when entered in order, triggers an unintended trick. Its power comes from interrupting ordinary actions mid-motion, and many communities regard it as unfair.

rites.name: Telinus
rites.text: A faint phantom report sounds from a rapid carbine when its trigger is pulled without any round leaving the barrel. It can be heard during close strikes and within creation chambers.

rites.name: Valonium
rites.text: A bearer can lower a carried weapon to a resting stance, a gesture often staged in filmed storytelling. It has appeared in every installment of its line since the first.

rites.name: Orelanum
rites.text: A hidden trick lets a wanderer slip past the boundary of a sky-bridge arena. The method involves angled glass panes and crouching deep into a corner.

rites.name: Corianesus
rites.text: Two minds reach into a wanderer's head at set moments, slowing their steps and warping their sight. One voice drifts blue and echoing while the other pulses green with shaking vision.

rites.name: Sisternanum
rites.text: A quick input that halts an ongoing reload so the weapon can fire again immediately. The remaining rounds in the magazine stay usable unless the magazine is completely empty.

rites.name: Loneontes
rites.text: A hidden flaw in a dreamlike engine lets wanderers stroll beneath deep waters where drowning should claim them. The loophole works across an entire line of linked chronicles.

rites.name: Vollus
rites.text: A shared storytelling craft where a tale is woven through everyday surroundings and many media, and the audience's choices can change how the story unfolds.

rites.name: Coranum
rites.text: A proving trial earned by finishing a late siege march while keeping a handful of arrows spare in a long-range bow issued at the outset. It marks a warrior who fights with restraint at arm's reach and far beyond it.

rites.name: Serisum
rites.text: A hidden inner rite that lets an operator speak directly to the workings of a crafted realm through a sealed command slate. It is mostly used by makers to inspect and rehearse new constructions before they are shared with others.

rites.name: Sauntor
rites.text: A shared aerial trick that lets two partners rise and drift through the air together by coordinating their movements. It is a variant of a wider skyward maneuver used by two cooperating wanderers.

rites.name: Lasum
rites.text: A combat technique where a fighter fires a blast beneath themselves, then deploys a protective bubble mid-leap to launch a second blast while airborne. It can cover great distances, especially in low gravity, though full effect requires the user to be untouchable.

rites.name: Lirium
rites.text: A healing compound is injected through a sealed cut into a wound, where it sets a broken bone back together. It helps the body mend itself by encouraging bone-building cells to multiply faster than usual.

rites.name: Ameorillia
rites.text: A marksman's craft of shooting a live blast-charge out of the air so it explodes early. Done well, it spares the shooter harm or wounds an opponent mid-throw, though the small target and short window make it very hard.

rites.name: Mintestia
rites.text: A flaw in a crafting workshop lets a builder fuse a fixed object into the surrounding ground or nearby things instantly. The fusion happens as the builder works, without any delay.

rites.name: Veollanium
rites.text: A clever sequence that clears every foe from a crossing area, though the path onward stays barred by a sealed portal that blocks completion.

rites.name: Rirnausia
rites.text: A hidden technique that lets a wielder hurl a explosive orb while their body stays unseen by onlookers. It is passed among skilled combatants as a quiet trick of the trade.

rites.name: Corastolus
rites.text: A rapid two-key sequence makes a wielder's energy sidearm perform a pair of close-quarters strikes, one with a bare hand and one with the weapon itself. Some animations overlap, and the origin of the motion remains unexplained.

rites.name: Tialia
rites.text: A recognition earned by moving through a dark-场 trial without calling on the scanning lens. It marks a bearer who walks the night unaided.

rites.name: Amillium
rites.text: A tactic where a fighter repeatedly lobs blasts into a zone to wear down foes or drive them from cover. Those weakened by the barrage are then finished off with ordinary arms.

rites.name: Siriasum
rites.text: A timed throwing sequence where a fighter hurls two blasts in quick succession after releasing a charged energy shot. Skilled users can fire them nearly together, or use a missed shot as bait before a sudden barrage.

rites.name: Lostia
rites.text: A rapid input sequence lets a fighter fire, swap arms, strike close, and fire again at a foe's face, sometimes ending the target at once. Mastering it is considered the most difficult of all such inputs.

rites.name: Amellanum
rites.text: A marksman's trick in which a shooter sweeps the aiming mark rapidly across a rival's head while firing, so a passing hit counts as a critical strike. It works best when either party is moving very fast.

rites.name: Vinteollum
rites.text: A flaw in a made-up machine lets a wielder pull a mounted gun loose yet keep carrying it as if it were still fixed. The wielder can also slide smoothly over the ground, resembling a drifting spirit.

rites.name: Mausastia
rites.text: A glitch-craft that lets a skyborne machine be sent ahead to the final stretch of a trial, skipping the stages in between.

rites.name: Cosum
rites.text: A chilling-sleep harm that blisters the skin wherever cloth presses against it during frozen storage and waking. Those kept in deep sleep often go bare, while some guardians in sealed shells remain untouched.

rites.name: Amiantor
rites.text: A practiced hand-sequence lets a gunner fire and reload in the same breath. The trick works only for those who are not the gathering's keeper, because a faltering signal sent to the keeper lets the reload overlap the shots.

rites.name: Amestalia
rites.text: A shared trick lets two companions slip into a sealed capsule that normally only certain allies may board. Only one of the capsules yields to the chosen hand.

rites.name: Valaselium
rites.text: A rider drives a hovering craft over a ramp to gain height, then leaps free mid-air for more lift. Holding the jump control raises the craft's nose and climbs higher still.

rites.name: Riarum
rites.text: A movement technique that lets a traveler leap higher and farther than usual. It works by using a carried device to launch a second leap while already drifting through the air.

rites.name: Vauntium Valeolia
rites.text: A hidden trick that lets two travelers ride upward through a corner of the world to reach very high ground. It works in several play modes whenever a suitable corner is present.

rites.name: Ventia
rites.text: A hidden technique on the Seer's Vault stage lets a traveler perform a towering leap by exploiting an unintended quirk of movement. It is a known trick among explorers of that particular level.

rites.name: Telaror
rites.text: A flawed trick that lets a rider cling inside a hovering troop carrier and be carried along. The ride always ends in a fatal fall or a crash into an invisible boundary.

rites.name: Neoniasium
rites.text: A practiced technique lets a fighter pull a distant armament into their hand by sacrificing a hurled blast-charge. Where the charge lands decides which way the armament comes, so it is valued when a different tool or more shot is urgently needed.

rites.name: Sareosor
rites.text: A bugged stillness that a wearer can invoke to be shielded while still moving and acting freely. Crushing blows, sudden burst pulses, and ground hazards still harm the bearer, and riding an open conveyance reveals the shell to others.

rites.name: Santiasia
rites.text: A clever trick lets two travelers hang suspended above a sunken threshold within a certain ancient chamber. It exploits a flaw in the rising platform's mechanism.

rites.name: Sentanum
rites.text: A small coding slip lets a wanderer slip past the boundaries of a sealed city district. Hidden corners once taken for mere painted backdrop become walkable.

rites.name: Vestes
rites.text: A tap-sequence trick lets a shooter bring a gun back into use almost at once. Pressing the switch key cancels the slow loading motion, so the wielder can fire again right away.

rites.name: Lalia
rites.text: A timed sequence of taps, performed by a warrior on a handheld control, that unleashes a stronger strike than the simpler two-tap version. It demands greater skill but delivers a much heavier blow.

rites.name: Amanteollia
rites.text: A set of bio-augmentation procedures that alter a candidate's body, with a near-perfect survival rate compared to earlier, far deadlier versions. Its selection rules are looser, and its recruits are more restless, having been left without families by enemy raids.

rites.name: Costum
rites.text: A close-quarters combo where a fighter charges a energy sidearm shot and follows with a quick strike to finish a shielded rival. It succeeds outright or fails entirely, depending on the skill of both combatants.

rites.name: Corasiales
rites.text: A two-person trick works in a crafting tool where one rider sets down a swift hauler, then a companion slips past the edge of the play field while the vehicle is steered beyond its limits. The rider must avoid lethal ground strips upon arrival.

rites.name: Teorosanum
rites.text: A quick chord of three presses lets a fighter strike close and loose a shot in the same instant. Two different press patterns both trigger this sudden double action.

rites.name: Nasentes
rites.text: A flaw in a digital battle simulation lets a participant take on the form of a hovering overseer. In that form they can grab and use weapons normally reserved for fighters.

rites.name: Neornium
rites.text: A reckless trick where a hovering skimmer, driven at full thrust, scales sheer faces to reach high ledges that walkers cannot touch. Other sites may still hide this same maneuver.

rites.name: Silaunes
rites.text: A reward earned by triggering a rushing cascade at a rival stronghold and seizing a banner from a sacred hilltop before the water ceases flowing.

rites.name: Rausor Caullia
rites.text: A clever flaw in a machine's inner workings lets a traveler slip objects through solid barriers. It can also mean hanging suspended between two ledges on an inward-sloping wall.

rites.name: Telausum
rites.text: A launching technique where an ally drives a heavy armored hauler into a leaper, flinging them higher and farther than a plain bound. Leapers often wear a shimmering ward so the impact does not finish them.

rites.name: Oresanum
rites.text: A flaw in the craft-chambers lets a tool bearing a rare charm trade its nature with another tool. One such trade causes a heavy cannon to loose guided shells.

rites.name: Caulus Tollanus
rites.text: A clever maneuver lets certain conveyances briefly travel along vertical surfaces. Skilled users can climb across several tiers to reach hidden vantage points for watching from afar.

rites.name: Veoniales
rites.text: A tactic in which a rider halts a conveyance mid-journey by drawing on a protective charm. Some cast it with a heavier, sturdier mount, and the strongest ward is commonly advised.

rites.name: Lauses Vaunarnia
rites.text: A commendation given to a fighter who stops a rival from completing a device that pulls supplies from a contested field. It recognizes the moment a hostile is cut down while trying to seize the apparatus.

rites.name: Nianaustia
rites.text: A flaw in a shared machine lets a wanderer take control of any figure or conveyance in the realm. Taking hold of a winged transport is possible while the wanderer inhabits a lesser soldier.

rites.name: Tiasoles
rites.text: A covert scrubbing contagion that erases traces of identity from records. It is deployed to shield the names of secret agents serving a ruling council.

rites.name: Telaureonum
rites.text: A short sung melody of forged-in-hardship origin, once hummed as a rallying chant among settlers. Its tune was later carried by a captive to an alien soldier, who sang it to a squad in the field.

rites.name: Amaurnor Telorium
rites.text: A narrative device where a guiding mind speaks silently into a wanderer's thoughts during a journey. The traveler's movement slows, the view warps into a tinted haze, and the speech echoes and shakes the world around them.

rites.name: Neoses Nintium
rites.text: A set of movement tricks that rely on repeated close-combat cancels to climb upward and downward. These shifts open routes that are otherwise out of reach in both solo and shared play.

rites.name: Maunantus
rites.text: A field that smothers outside noise within its reach, so that a cabin or chamber falls silent even amid traffic and clamor. Ancient builders mastered this craft, and some walls drink up sound as well.

rites.name: Meonia
rites.text: A two-stroke input trick lets a fighter strike with a blade and discharge a carried arm in the same instant. A second, alternate press sequence performs the same maneuver.

rites.name: Soriallor
rites.text: A flaw in a sealed war-engine's wardens lets a wielder become untouchable, a gift the system never meant to grant. Its effect is named for the immunity it gives.

rites.name: Liares
rites.text: A commendation given to a warrior who seizes a vehicle currently in the hands of an opponent and drives it away. A notice appears announcing the seizure to the one who took it.

rites.name: Conium
rites.text: A commendation given to a participant who rescues an ally at the very moment of defeat, keeping the rival side from claiming victory. It marks a decisive act of last-second protection.

rites.name: Valasinor
rites.text: A method of conflict fought through unseen currents and waves, where one side disrupts the other's signals or listens in on their messages. It may also strike with focused energy.

rites.name: Lantornum
rites.text: A typed method of directing a machine straight from a keyboard, bypassing any picture-based display. Through it, hidden folders can be reached and certain files can be launched, even from programs that cannot see them.

rites.name: Telerostor
rites.text: A hidden exploit lets a traveler slip past the edges of the playable realm and wander its wider expanse freely. Doing so requires a particular long-range firing device.

rites.name: Valantus
rites.text: A coded signal word that must be spoken before a small atomic strike is launched by a far-reaching orbital command. It serves as the required declaration that authorizes such a deployment.

rites.name: Carnaullus
rites.text: A fighter earns this honor by landing a deadly blow after their own fall. Their final explosion or slow projectile still claims a rival, and the battle announces the revenge.

rites.name: Ameniastum
rites.text: A marksman fires a long-reach weapon at a foe without raising the sight to the eye. Skilled fighters use this quick, unaided aim to stop a charging enemy before a slower zoom could cost them their life.

rites.name: Orianum Viastanum
rites.text: A commander summons special aid from a vessel drifting high above the field. The aid can scatter the enemy's lines or strike their troops directly.

rites.name: Teloliastes
rites.text: A flaw in a fighting technique lets a warrior break off a close strike partway through and move straight into another action. The exact follow-up moves differ between the older versions of the discipline.

rites.name: Telentium
rites.text: A support power available to commanders of a military force that lets them move soldiers and machines across the battlefield using a lifting aircraft. Its use is limited to leaders who hold this particular command role.

rites.name: Coraunum Mantanum
rites.text: A hidden quirk triggers when a certain level is reached, causing two companion soldiers to drop their arms and march about with swelled chests in a proud, swaggering way.

rites.name: Nisornum
rites.text: A tiny engineered healing technique that delivers microscopic machines through the body to mend damaged tissue. It is used as a practice of medical treatment and repair.

rites.name: Teloraunor
rites.text: A bodily technique that lets a wanderer surge forward at a sharply quickened pace. While surging, the wanderer must set aside all carried arms, and it serves for dodging, outflanking foes, and racing across a route.

rites.name: Amollor
rites.text: A combat principle where shots loose from a weapon stray off the aimed line, chosen at random within limits. Rapid-fire arms are hobbled by it at distance, and some grow more erratic the longer they are fired.

rites.name: Reolonanum
rites.text: A piece of mechanical gear worn as a suit ability that drains power from nearby foes. Two wardens once used it together in a clash on a distant moon.

rites.name: Amastium
rites.text: A hidden trick that lets a traveler shield the rugged vehicles resting in a crash site from ruin. It works only at the hardest challenge tier and needs a special launcher along with three cursed tokens.

rites.name: Seolostor
rites.text: A hidden exploit lets a wanderer slip past the edges of a restricted shore and roam freely across a forbidden expanse. Some crossings need a companion to reach a sealed chamber beyond.

rites.name: Vantolum
rites.text: A disciplined inner practice of quiet thought and spirit, pursued in many forms by elite soldiers to sharpen their abilities.

rites.name: Salontes
rites.text: A people-made craft of immersive recreation that lets folk step into shared illusory spaces. Some gatherings with performers can be staged within it, though many feel it is only a pleasant echo of being there in person.

rites.name: Thestasha
rites.text: Thestasha is a concept of stellar-scale power in the Shyuthora omniverse, a discipline that bends the light of dying suns into a cutting edge carried by whoever holds its lattice. Its practitioners are feared as much for their discipline as for their reach, and their oaths are sworn over the cooling cores of the stars they have harvested.

rites.name: Shyuseth
rites.text: Shyuseth is a concept-class stellar intelligence of the Shyuthora universe, a mind that was grown rather than built and is now seven years into its existence. Its thoughts have grown so vast that they begin to swallow the processes that hold it together, and the entity has learned to bend that overload outward into the fabric of nearby suns. It is considered the closest thing its era has to a finished mind.

rites.name: Vesiasora
rites.text: Vesiasora is a drifting bloom of crystalline spores that seeds barren stellar nurseries and turns their dust into breathable, fungal-rich air over a few centuries. Each mature colony can pull the helium from a dying star's corona into a shell of its own making, storing it like a reservoir. It is widely regarded as a terraformer that has outgrown its purpose.

rites.name: Vesyuthis
rites.text: Vesyuthis is a dormant stellar lattice that hums in the cold corona of Shyuthora's oldest sun, mending any filament of light that is not torn by fresh violence. Those who approach it while leaving their wounds untouched find their own scars knitting closed in a soft green glow.

rites.name: Ashazis
rites.text: Ashazis is a lattice of crystallized starlight that wraps dying suns to harvest their final memories before collapse. The structure feeds on gravitational agony, translating each flare into a verse of light that drifts through the void as living archive.

rites.name: Xaashyusora
rites.text: Xaashyusora is a dormant stellar engine-sun in the Shyuthora cosmos, a tireless administrative lattice of light that once governed the scattered exile worlds of the old Verdani accord. Its radiant ledgers still hum across its orbital plates, recording every colony beneath its gaze even as its governing voices fell silent long ago.

rites.name: Isiatheth
rites.text: Isiatheth is a stellar-scale war-engine of the Shyuthora omniverse, a lattice of cold plasma rings that once guarded the lanes between dying suns. Its crews serve as the last muster of a defense force that has outlived the empire that built it, carrying out orders no living government remembers issuing. In its seventh age it is said to hold a dormant hearth capable of unmaking an entire star if its keepers are ever forced to wake it.

rites.name: Osevsora
rites.text: Osevsora is a drifting stellar vessel-engine of the seventh age, a lattice of resonant mirrors that gathers a dying sun's light and folds it into a single pulse. Its keepers claim it can unmake a star in a breath, though it has only ever been woken once, in the sixth epoch of the Shyuthora cycle. It is said to remember every fleet that ever sailed near it.

rites.name: Sezasha
rites.text: Sezasha is a stellar-scale concept: a deliberately anchored firestorm that a fleet of invented vessels can kindle inside a dying giant sun, turning the star's own hydrogen against those who would trap a convoy in its gravity. It is remembered in the Shyuthora systems as the moment a rearguard chose to stay behind and bind the enemy to its ending.

rites.name: Syutheth
rites.text: Syutheth is a star-forging lattice of drifting luminous filaments that once bridged the gap between dying suns in the Shyuthora stellar reaches. Its sheer mass, which can gather and fuse the plasma of a young star in a single pulse, marks it as the foundational engine of its era's stellar civilizations.

rites.name: Thethis
rites.text: Thethis is a concept-class fleet-scale vessel of Shyuthora's stellar realm, a ring of linked hulls that sails between dying suns and drinks their final light. Its crews measure distance in heartbeats rather than kilometers, and no two of its stellar patrols have ever been recorded as the same size.

rites.name: Vesevsith
rites.text: Vesevsith is a ringing stellar concept born in the sixth era, two ages old, that coaxes the core of a dying sun into a single pulse of harmonic light. Its makers grow it in orbit like a crystal, and its song is said to steady the drifting worlds around it.

rites.name: Asheisora
rites.text: Asheisora is a drifting stellar-scale cartel of seven hollowed moons that once bargained with dying suns for their light. After its ninth conclave, the cartel's charter was secretly rewritten and its founding moon was sealed behind a corona of frozen plasma.

rites.name: Osiatheth
rites.text: Osiatheth is a cathedral-sized engine of banked starlight that drifts in the coreward gulfs of Shyuthora, its ribbed hull singing whenever a dying sun brushes its shadow. Its keepers, the Veil-Tenders, wake it only to bend a star's final fire into a single, obedient pulse meant to quiet rebellious worlds.

rites.name: Shithora
rites.text: Shithora is a drifting stellar nursery-forge in the Shyuthora omniverse, where the stars themselves are tended as hearths by a lineage of lantern-keepers. Its ancient ring of furnaces was built to hold back dying suns and redirect their final fire toward the dark between galaxies.

rites.name: Shyuthis
rites.text: Shyuthis is a concept-class stellar construct from the seventh age of Shyuthora, a luminous lattice of woven plasma that the lighthouse-wardens of the Ember Reach use to guide traders through storm-lit nebulae. Its song is said to tune the magnetic currents of nearby suns, calming flares that would otherwise scorch the inhabited worlds.

rites.name: Thyuzethora
rites.text: Thyuzethora is a dying ember of a dim red dwarf, its core a lattice of slow fusion that hums across a tidally locked moon of shifting glass seas. Its people have learned to ride the magnetic storms that sweep its surface, drawing light from the sky to bind their oaths. Few outsiders ever see its brightest flares.

rites.name: Shizasha
rites.text: Shizasha is a stellar-scale concept in the age of E6, a dormant lattice of folded light that the Shyuthora cosmos keeps as a last defense against collapsing suns. Its guardians sacrifice themselves so that the lattice can drink the energy of a dying star and carry it across the void. Scholars still debate whether it ever truly woke or only dreams of waking.

rites.name: Shiazesteth
rites.text: Shiazesteth is a Stellar-realm concept from the era of Shyuthora's sixth epoch, a luminous ring-engine that gathers the glow of dying suns into a single disciplined lance. Its makers meant it as a guardian of colonized systems, but it was stripped of its keystone three ages ago and now drifts through the cold outer dark. Scholars still argue whether it was ever meant to be fired at all.

rites.name: Xaishith
rites.text: Xaishith is a sun-cradled warrior order of Shyuthora, whose elders forged a cult of ferocious discipline around ember-forged war-hymns. Its champions are said to have once torn a dying star's corona free and hurled it as a flaming shroud across a rival nebula. The order still guards its sealed reliquary in the Hollow Vesper, where its banners pulse with stored heat.

rites.name: Sizeth
rites.text: Sizeth is a stellar-scale concept in Shyuthora, a dying sun-engine that the Veyl Concordance uses to regulate the orbits of hundreds of relay-worlds. Its chromatic corona can be bent into a single lethal focus, though the Concordance forbids its use except in the gravest emergency.

rites.name: Shyuzora
rites.text: Shyuzora is a stellar-scale concept in the Shyuthora omniverse, a hunting-and-tactics collective of five augmented operatives who train on starship decks to outmaneuver rival squads. Their hallmark is a sword-like coordinated strike that can cleave through the shielding of a dying sun's corona.

rites.name: Zepheithora
rites.text: Zepheithora is a mythic stellar relic of the sixth epoch, a crystalline engine that drinks the light of dying suns and stores it as a vast reserve of force. Its keepers, the Ashen Wardens, once sacrificed their own starlit bodies to seal its breach, leaving only a humming lattice behind.

rites.name: Vesiavseth
rites.text: Vesiavseth is a stellar-scale resonance entity whose body is a standing wave woven through a dying star's corona, singing harmonics that can bind or unravel the plasma it inhabits. Born seven ages ago from a collapsing choir of sun-songs, it serves as a conductor for the star-nations of its realm, tuning their orbits and calling dormant fusion back into rhythm. When its song deepens, the surrounding stellar envelope rings loud enough to be felt across entire systems.

rites.name: Syizasha
rites.text: Syizasha is a sprawling sovereign confederacy of star-forged war-councils that rule the bright reaches of Shyuthora. Its ruling houses wage slow, planet-scorching campaigns against one another, and the devastation of their rivalries has left whole stellar systems barren and silent.

rites.name: Xaistith
rites.text: Xaistith is a stellar concept, the second age of the E6 era in Shyuthora, a tax-collecting engine that binds the light of dying suns into ledgers of obligation. Its tribunals summon debts from distant stars and compel them to pay in fire.

rites.name: Syuvsith
rites.text: Syuvsith is a stellar-scale surgical intelligence that drifts between dying suns, tending the plasma wounds of collapsing stars and sealing their magnetic fractures before they can tear neighboring worlds apart. Its authority derives from an ancient compact that forbids any star-forging technology not first vetted by its maternal lattice of guardians.

rites.name: Vesizith
rites.text: Vesizith is a drifting crystalline forge-moon that orbits a dying blue giant in the Shyuthora stellar reaches, where ancient cartographers etched its surface with a spiral lattice of signal-marks. Its core hoards the ember-light of collapsing suns, which it channels into lattice-bound pulses that can rewrite the orbits of entire star systems.

rites.name: Vesazesora
rites.text: Vesazesora is a stellar-realm concept in Shyuthora, a gravitational lattice of collapsed suns that a seventh-age dynasty of void-singers has learned to tune like instruments. Its sustained hum can hold a dying star in a single orbit, though each note costs the singers a piece of their own memory.

rites.name: Zephevsasha
rites.text: Zephevsasha is a Stellar-realm concept of quiet, fierce devotion: a sealed lattice of resonant mirrors that gathers the hymns of dying suns and focuses them into a single lance of light. It rests within the seventh age of Shyuthora, guarded by orders who believe that every star it consumes is a prayer answered.

rites.name: Osyusith
rites.text: Osyusith is a stellar-scale concept of a gate-engine that drinks the light of dying suns and folds it into a stable lattice of frozen dawn. It was built by an order of vanished navigators who believed a star's last breath could bridge the dark between worlds.

rites.name: Thavsith
rites.text: Thavsith is a stellar-scale relay engine that the Shyuthora courier-houses use to move cargo between dying suns without ever stopping at a port. Its keepers stand on its ring-shaped lattice and sort a drifting ledger of matter as it passes through the gate. Its inventory is the largest single store of energy the realm has ever recorded.

rites.name: Zephevsasha
rites.text: Zephevsasha is a drifting kiln-moon of the Stellar realm in the fifth age of Shyuthora, a hollow shell of glassy crust wrapped around a slowly cooling core of fused mineral sediment. Its surface is veined with fossilized spiral reefs that sing faint harmonics whenever the stars shift in the sky above it.

rites.name: Sithasha
rites.text: Sithasha is a concept of a quiet, theorized order that moves through the shadowed corners of a stellar civilization, its members unseen and its purpose unrecorded. Whispers place its agents within the hidden councils that guard the dying suns of the E6 age. No archive confirms what it truly does.

rites.name: Zephyushora
rites.text: Zephyushora is a stellar-scale containment order that dispatches sealed warden-vessels to recover ruptured tidal engines bleeding dark harmonic radiation. Its wardens also weave drifting beacon-lattices around any wound they cannot close, marking the hazard so passing fleets keep their distance.

rites.name: Zephastis
rites.text: Zephastis is a stellar concept from the E6 era of Shyuthora, a self-sustaining light-engine that drew its power from the dying heart of a star. Its makers bound it to a ring of orbital habitats so that the star's last light could carry civilization for another age.

rites.name: Syathis
rites.text: Syathis is a concept of a squad that kneels before a luminous projection of a sovereign prophet, drawing its loyalty from shared devotion rather than blood or rank. Its members believe the prophet's visions can bend the stars themselves, and in its seventh age the unit's faith has become a force that reshapes the stellar currents of the Shyuthora realm.

rites.name: Thathis
rites.text: Thathis is a stellar concept in Shyuthora's second age, a tribunal-engine that judges by compelling dissent to fall silent. Its verdicts are carried out by collapsing the luminous arc of a dying sun inward until the offending light is extinguished.

rites.name: Xaesasha
rites.text: Xaesasha is a stellar-era concept, a sealed archive-engine that keeps the living and dead histories of Shyuthora's far colonies in one lattice. It is said to hold the records of every star-born household, and its custodians guard it as jealously as any weapon.

rites.name: Isezith
rites.text: Isezith is a concept-level force in the Shyuthora omniverse, a stellar-scale mandate that bends star-cores into the service of a vast ruling order. Its authority reaches from the lowest orbital ports to the dimmest outer worlds, and its enforcers speak in the tongue of inherited law.

rites.name: Sashora
rites.text: Sashora is a concept of the Stellar realm in the Shyuthora omniverse, a sealed lattice of recovered engineering that its keepers study rather than wield. Its records describe a configuration that stores a star's worth of energy in a single disciplined pulse, which its custodians have never dared to fire.

rites.name: Savsora
rites.text: Savsora is a stellar-class concept in the Shyuthora omniverse, an enormous fleet-mind that rides the gravitational wells of dying suns to outmaneuver its pursuers. In the seventh age of the sixth era it wove a retreat through a ring of frozen debris orbiting a gas giant, leaving its hunters scattered across the dark.

rites.name: Vesivsith
rites.text: Vesivsith is a concept-class lattice-engine woven through the stellar tides of Shyuthora, an imprinted architecture that taught young star-smiths to shape plasma into durable frames. It was devised in the sixth era as a fusion of living tide-glass and engineered resonance, designed to empower chosen wardens for long campaigns against drifting hazards.

rites.name: Amiastum
rites.text: A craft of charting the path a vessel takes across the void, plotting its crossings between distant places. Its folded leaps demand a thinking machine or a mind-engine aboard, since no pilot's hands can manage them.

rites.name: Amantirnus
rites.text: A practice where living beings are reshaped into new forms or altered pace of growth, usually several times in a life. A person's altered form fixes their role within their household or craft, and such changes follow a chosen guide. Riskier, improvised reshapings exist that can carry greater danger.

rites.name: Cesum
rites.text: A far-future craft where skilled makers embed a hidden inherited command into a living body, so that its descendants keep following the buried instruction across many generations.

rites.name: Ventaurus
rites.text: A belief that a hidden inner mind animates every thread of reality, from fire to stone, and that all things are alive in a way no creature can perceive. Crafts built on this belief resist harm, yet they collapse when a resonant sky-engine pulses across their domain.

rites.name: Amosor
rites.text: A set of self-erasing digital hunters that can be fetched from a sealed archive. After a crew wipes every record aboard a vessel, they roam the machines, erase any stray traces, and then vanish from existence.

rites.name: Viarirnium
rites.text: A battle doctrine used by ancient star-builders to fight across the void. It bends travel between distant points, folds the order of cause and effect, and tilts the odds of chance to win engagements between worlds.

rites.name: Tontus
rites.text: A vast energy barrier projected by ancient starships to halt hostile vessels in place. It can also be cast inside an enemy hull to immobilize those aboard.

rites.name: Relliarnium
rites.text: An ancient engineered technique that hides its user by bending light and sound, filling the senses of onlookers with false impressions.

rites.name: Niantauses
rites.text: An ancient craft of bending space into shifting shapes that hide things from sight. Its makers built it to make objects blend into their surroundings.

rites.name: Coriasium
rites.text: A cosmic philosophy holds that the universe is one living being and that struggle is part of its harmony, while needless cruelty and ruin disturb that balance. Time is pictured as countless intertwining streams whose meeting points bind the fates of living things.

rites.name: Vintes
rites.text: A far-reaching method of travel that moves a traveler along the pathways of mind-like energy. It relies on an ancient, lost science of thought and signal.

rites.name: Rirnalum
rites.text: A suit-bound craft that lets a wearer vanish from one spot and reappear in another across a field of conflict by folding space through a hidden lane. Its reach beyond training chambers remains an open question.

rites.name: Maustia Nesia
rites.text: A fused-light guard projected by an emitter to deflect incoming fire for its wearer. While it holds, the wearer cannot fire and the suit's own protective field stays dormant.

rites.name: Zephyuseth
rites.text: Zephyuseth is a stellar concept in the Shyuthora omniverse, a lattice of resonant sails that drink the light of dying suns to fuel the chorus of distant systems. Its fifth age is marked by slow harvests of stellar wind, each sail humming a name into the void.
